notes.title: Massive update: Checkpoints, Endless Mode and Oculus Rift support!
notes.content:
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
Lockdown: Stand Alone received a big update today.
Alongside the much requested [b]checkpoint system[/b] comes official Oculus Rift support and
the hardcore [b]endless mode[/b].

[h1]Endless mode (Single-player)[/h1]
This mode brings a more traditional wave shooting mechanism to
the game while still maintaining the freedom of movement you've familiarized yourself with.
Compete in online leaderboards on who can kill the most enemies. I can assure you that this gamemode isn't too easy.
Ammunition is more scarce and you will receive more ammo via helicopter drops every other wave. Sidearms play a lot larger role in this gamemode than in single player.

Endless Mode can be accessed from the main menu.

[h1]Oculus Rift support[/h1]
Oculus Rift users can now jump in and enjoy Lockdown: Stand Alone. Room-scale is not required and the assisted rotation feature can be used with a 180-degree tracking setup.

[h1]Checkpoints[/h1]
Checkpoints are fixed areas in the level where you will be brought back when you die. Level progress is not reset, so enemies you've killed will stay dead and if you've collected any items, you will keep them.

Your indie developer,
Anton Korhonen

notes.title: Update released
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

This update balances the difficulty and brings improvements to the visuals and gameplay elements.

[h1] Performance and visual improvements [/h1]
- Single-pass stereo rendering is now enabled, which should improve GPU performance up to 20%
- Shaders rewritten to support the aforementioned feature
- Visibility improved for large scenes

[h1] Added the seventh level [/h1]
Step inside the tunnels that lead to the Dominus building. 

[h1] Added two new weapons [/h1]
Clear your way with a M249 (main weapon) and new sidearm (UMP). 
Both are fully automatic and bring much requested balance for the battle against the aberrations.

[h1] Additional gameplay improvements [/h1]
- Dead enemies can now be shot through which effectively lowers the steep difficulty of the game a little
- Enemy muscle weight and pinning adjusted for more realistic ragdolls and movement

Your indie developer,
Anton

notes.title: Performance update
notes.content:
Hey!

After receiving some complaints about the game not running well on AMD processors (most notably FX8320/FX8350) combined with great GPUs (980Ti/1070/1080), i started to work on optimizations.

[h1] GPU skinning [/h1]
This effectively directs the mesh skinning workload from the CPU to the GPU.

[h1] Enemy pathfinding improved [/h1]
The pathfinding has been slightly optimized. The CPU workload should be about 10% less with this update.

[h1] Blend weights [/h1]
I've managed to cut the performance impact a little by halving the blend weight count from four to two.

[h1] Improved lighting and shadow performance [/h1]
More baked lights instead of realtime lighting. I've also adjusted the shadow resolution inside the levels to reflect these changes.

[b]These changes should bring the overall performance boost up to 15-20 %.[/b]
The game is still heavy on the CPU so i cannot (yet) lower the minimum requirements. 

As always - if you have any feedback - head over to the discussions, send a friend request or e-mail me at anton.korhonen@viversion.com

Your indie developer,
Anton

notes.title: Left handed support is here!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

I have released a patch which enables left handed support and brings some bug fixes to the game.

[h1] Left handed support [/h1]
Go to the options menu and tick "Left handed". Note that this requires a scene reload every time when changed.
This reflectively mirrors the button layout for teleportation etc.

[h1] Added the option to enable/disable touchpad movement [/h1]
Options menu now shows the option "Trackpad movement by touch".
If enabled, you can move the player only by sliding your finger with the touchpad.
The default behaviour requires the touchpad to be pressed for moving the player. This way any accidental touchpad presses when using the teleport can be avoided.

[h1] Supersampling is restricted to 1.5 [/h1]
As i've received complaints that the game is running slow with large supersample values, i've restricted it to maximum of 1.5.
[b] NOTE: Using the supersampling slider requires a powerful GPU. Anything above 1.2 requires a GTX 1080. [/b]

More patch notes:
- Adjusted ambient lighting by +10%
- Direction shift now has a 25% smaller margin
- Height adjustment allows for a 10% larger height
- Raycast item grabbing support for left handed

If you have any feedback, head over to discussions or contact me at anton.korhonen@viversion.com

Your indie developer,
Anton

notes.title: Patch released: Height adjustment and raycast item grabbing!
notes.content:
After some heavy development and testing the sitting experience is now refined!

[h1] Height adjustment [/h1]
You can now adjust your height from the options menu when sitting.
This is a slider and you can see the change in height real-time.

[h1] Raycast item grab [/h1]
By enabling "Ray grab items" from the options menu, you can hold the grip button to fire a visible ray from your left hand. This ray can be used to pick up magazines and other items from the world.
This is very useful for a sitting experience.

Weapons still have to be picked up from tables with the right hand, but
we've developed the levels this in mind, so it should not be a problem.

Upcoming soon:
- Left handed support
- Easing the weapon reload mechanics for disabled users
- The next level which is set in a destroyed underground metro system

As always, head over to the discussions if you have any feedback or e-mail me at anton.korhonen@viversion.com 

Best regards,
Anton

notes.title: Locomotion update
notes.content:
When using the trackpad to move, the movement direction was calculated 
relative to the headset orientation. Basically good if you're always facing the direction you're going.

This is now updated to work "Onward" style, where the movement direction is calculated relative to the controller orientation.

No more throwing up! :)

Your indie developer,
Anton

notes.title: Patch released: Important bug fixes and improvements
notes.content:
I've released a patch that fixes a couple of issues:

[h1] Magazines can now be holstered back [/h1]
You just took out that mag and you realize you don't need to reload just yet?
Just keep holding it in your hand and put it back. Already dropped it? Just pick it up from the floor.
Dropped magazines from weapons are still lost, but this way you don't lose the precious full ones!

[h1] .50 cal machine guns are now easier to use [/h1]
The hands now lock to the turrent until you move them about three feet (1 metre) away from it. This helps in using the turret a lot and the hands no longer should snap out of it even if you move a lot.

[h1] Improved the game pause function [/h1]
Now you can pause the game very easily as the watch responds to the whole finger instead of only the fingertip.

Complete sitting experience for disabled users is coming this week and left handed support later this month!

Also the next campaign level is on the works! Stay tuned!

Your humble developer,
Anton

notes.title: Patch released: The highly requested health system is here!
notes.content:
[h1] Now you can take three hits before dying [/h1]
Your screen will fade a little every time you take a hit and it will take four seconds to recharge a single hitpoint.

[h1] Flare launcher enabled for Level 3 and onwards [/h1]
Fire a flare on the ground and watch as the creatures arrive.

[h1] Touchpad movement speed refined [/h1]
You could move way too fast before. Now we're modified the movement speed to get a more lifelike experience.

As always, if you have any feedback, head over to the discussions or drop a message to anton.korhonen@viversion.com.

We are always actively updating the game!
Happy hunting!

Best regards,
Anton
